{"content": "1|# Hermes Agent config for one headless trial on a Particle cell (HARN-16).
2|# Copied to $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (under /harness-state) by adapter.sh when
3|# HE_MODEL_BASE_URL ends in /particle. Particle speaks OpenAI Chat Completions,
4|# so the model runs on Hermes's custom-endpoint provider (transport
5|# chat_completions) through the custom_providers entry below; the adapter
6|# selects it with --provider custom:particle. Secrets are not here: the adapter
7|# exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the per-trial proxy token) and OPENAI_BASE_URL (the
8|# proxy plus /v1), which Hermes expands into this file at load time. On a
9|# custom endpoint Hermes sends no reasoning field and no output cap of its own,
10|# so extra_body adds both to every request: reasoning_effort medium, the value
11|# every harness on the cell sends (Particle serves medium at its high tier),
12|# and max_completion_tokens 128000, the cap the OpenAI cells run under, because
13|# Particle spends output on reasoning_content before any visible text.
14|# Everything else is as in config.yaml.
15|_config_version: 46
16|
17|model:
18|  provider: "custom:particle"
19|  default: "particle-1"
20|  base_url: "${OPENAI_BASE_URL}"
21|  # Particle-1's window (docs.particle.ai/models), as the OpenClaw and QM Particle configs declare it. Without it Hermes asks
22|  # the endpoint's /models and falls back to 256,000 (agent/model_metadata.py), so it would compress at a quarter of the window.
23|  context_length: 1048576
24|
25|custom_providers:
26|  - name: "particle"
27|    base_url: "${OPENAI_BASE_URL}"
28|    key_env: "OPENAI_API_KEY"
29|    extra_body:
30|      reasoning_effort: "medium"
31|      max_completion_tokens: 128000
32|

35|  cwd: "/workspace"

42|# Nothing that needs a person: no update checks, no telemetry prompts.

44|check_for_updates: false

46|# No lazy pip installs at turn time (Bedrock's boto3, edge-tts): the trial

- Correction to my last report: the `mcp` package *is* installed — in Hermes's own venv (`mcp-2.0.0`). I'd checked only the system python. So wiring was available and I was wrong to call it blocked.
- I first registered `--command /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain`, and `hermes mcp test` said connected. It was broken anyway. That launcher is a `#!/usr/bin/env bun` script, and Hermes hands MCP subprocesses a filtered PATH that excludes `~/.bun/bin`. Under `env -i PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` it dies with `env: 'bun': No such file or directory`. It would have failed on every future session while looking correctly configured — the test passed only because it inherited my shell's full PATH.
- Fixed: the entry now runs `/harness-state/.bun/bin/bun /harness-state/gbrain/src/cli.ts serve …` with an explicit `env.PATH` override, so resolution doesn't depend on the launcher's shebang.
- Verified by a real MCP round trip through that exact command under a Hermes-like filtered env: initialize → tools/list (8) → `remember` → `recall`. The fact persisted to the DB and read back.

One caveat worth your attention
This sandbox's config.yaml is regenerated by adapter.sh at the start of each trial — the file's own header says so. The `mcp_servers` block I added lives in that file, so it may not survive into the next trial. If gbrain tools go missing later, that's the cause; re-running `hermes mcp add` with the same args restores it. Tools also need a new session to appear — they won't show up mid-conversation.
